review_plan.coordinator_prior: Recorded BEFORE any reviewer of this round ran, and deliberately falsifiable. (1) I expect J1 to find the run set formally complete -- eight enumerated runs, the nested run: record schema [SR-3] with command.txt and environment.json companions, and seeds exactly 760806 (R3 and R4), 760810 (R5), 760812 (R7), 760808 (R8) as declared -- and to find one provenance defect I am pre-committing to rather than discovering afterwards: execution-report.yaml declares resolved_model_id cursor-grok-4.6 with model_verified false, fallback_used true and git_dirty_at_runs true. That is a provenance finding, never a defect in the mathematics. (2) I expect J2 to confirm R4 == R3 on the instance list and on counted ops (9191003 both). THE SINGLE MOST DANGEROUS ITEM IN THE PACKAGE is R4's raw iv2_counts_identical: false against the report's prose that the counts agree after JSON serialization. My prior is that the producer's explanation (int-keyed versus str-keyed dicts compared before dump) is CORRECT -- AND THIS IS THE PLACE I MOST EXPECT TO BE WRONG. A raw record saying false while a summary says identical is precisely the shape of a re-scored run; any divergence beyond dict-key typing means IV-2 fails and, by the frozen invalidation rules, the R3 and R5 readings are void. (3) I expect J2 to recompute ops_cap_respected as the EXACT boolean (counted_ops < 1.0e8) required by [SR-9], with no tolerance band, and to find it false for R5 alone (100002120 >= 1.0e8) and true for the other seven. I expect R5's found = 0 to be INERT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- it stopped at b_index 666 of 10000 and says nothing about n = 8 either way. (4) IV-1 IS WHERE I EXPECT THIS ROUND TO BREAK, and I record that before either report returns. The frozen control fixes certified totals on the known-false d = (1, 1, ...) family at n - 1 (5 at n=6, 7 at n=8) and says IV-1 failure voids ALL runs. The record shows NO BUILD AT ALL at n=6 on all eight tuples (degenerate_deg_s_2) and [5, 6, 7, 7, 7, 7, 6, 7] against expected 7 at n=8, with n8_all_match false. My prior is that IV-1 as frozen is NOT satisfied. I am not deciding that and neither reviewer is asked to: J3 establishes the exact recorded verdict against the frozen text, J5 establishes whether the control discriminates at all, and only a later Coordinator decision composes them. If IV-1 did fail, the correct reading is that the run set is invalid or infrastructure-limited under core rule 3 -- NOT that anything about HEUR-1 was learned. (5) I expect J5 to find that IV-3 / R8 DID NOT DISCRIMINATE: 0 of 9 plants were built, recovered is 0/0 and the exponent gate never evaluated. A control that produced no objects cannot fail, which docs/inventor-protocol.md treats as the canonical artifact tell rather than a pass. (6) I expect J5 to find R6's zero weaker than it looks: found is [] but null_proof_first is null (PD-1), so the run does not itself exhibit the infeasibility proof the contract required to be frozen first, and the same degenerate_deg_s_2 rejection that emptied R7 and R8 is a live alternative explanation for an empty R6. (7) I expect J6 to find PD-3 material: the n=8 Bezout enumeration used the integer (a, b) box of width min(H, 20) rather than the full rational height-H coefficient lattice, so R5 did not measure the quantity the frozen contract defines, independently of the exhaustion. (8) I expect J4 to REPRODUCE {100: 15, 1000: 22, 10000: 28} and feasibility fraction 0.002 from the contract statement alone. That is my prior and the one I would most like overturned: a blind disagreement localises to one of two named implementations and is worth more than the agreement. (9) I expect J6 to find at least one cost-model gap: wall_seconds_monotonic and wall_seconds_timestamp_span are identical to six decimal places in every one of the eight runs, which is one instrument reported twice rather than the two independent measurements [SR-10] asks for; and the IC-1 exclusions mean counted_ops is a LOWER bound on true cost. (10) What would overturn the prior as a whole: a finding that R3's 28 certified instances were produced by a code path the controls never traverse. If the counted path and the control path differ, 28 has no positive control behind it and no reading of it survives, whatever its arithmetic. This prior is a pre-commitment, not an instruction. A reviewer that contradicts it has produced this round's most valuable output and must say so plainly.

joints.joint: J1 run-record integrity, schema conformance, seed integrity, and raw/summary agreement
joints.attack_plan: Re-parse all eight run directories under experiments/EXP-ECRANK-73275e/runs/ at snapshot 03c6e3181bc54b67ab3904b5f6187dbe4e6cb3ad against the AGENTS.md artifact policy and the frozen contract's required_artifacts [SR-3]: the nested run: record with RUN_REQUIRED_TOP (id, experiment_id, status, code, environment, inputs, timing, result), code.commit and code.command, the command.txt and environment.json companions, stdout.log, stderr.log, raw-result.json. Then RESOLVE iv2_counts_identical: false in R4's raw-result.json: reconstruct the comparison the producer made and decide whether it is a dict-key typing artifact as claimed or a real divergence. This single boolean is load-bearing -- IV-2 failure voids the R3 and R5 readings by the frozen invalidation rules. (b) OP ACCOUNTING. Recompute ops_cap_respected for all eight runs as the EXACT boolean (counted_ops < 1.0e8) required by [SR-9], with NO tolerance band, from the counted_ops in each raw-result.json; confirm the per-run values (R1 0, R2 0, R3 9191003, R4 9191003, R5 100002120, R6 37416, R7 308732, R8 6751) and the exact booleans, and state whether the recorded boolean matches your recomputation in every run. joints.joint: J3 recorded outcome of every control IV-1..IV-9 against its frozen text

joints.joint: J4 blind re-derivation of N_6(H) and the n = 6 feasibility fraction
joints.attack_plan: BEFORE opening any blind_from path, and before opening experiments/EXP-ECRANK-73275e/execution-report.yaml or the R3/R4 raw-result.json, implement FROM THE STATEMENT ALONE and write your numbers down. The statement: for n = 6 at seed 760806, over the declared 10^4 b-tuple sample (affine normal form b1 = 0, b2 = 1, b3..b6 distinct integers in [-20, 20] excluding {0, 1}, seeded order via random.Random(760806), no adaptive reordering), with the square pattern prescribed on the carrier coordinate r_n and support {-1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13}, solve the single (n - 5 = 1) quadratic ellipticity condition on g's coefficients exactly over Q inside the declared nested coefficient boxes H in {10^2, 10^3, 10^4}, and compute (i) construct_count N_6(H) -- the number of DISTINCT-MINIMAL-MODEL certified instances (nonsingular, twist class populated, certified rank above the trivial), cumulative at each H, exactly as metrics.primary defines it -- and (ii) the feasibility fraction, the fraction of b-tuples with at least one in-box solution. Use fractions.Fraction and the stdlib only; no PARI, no descent, no network. Write your values, the exact definition you implemented, and your read order into validation-report.md FIRST. ONLY THEN open the R3 raw-result.json and compare against the recorded {100: 15, 1000: 22, 10000: 28}, feasible_tuples 20 and feasibility_fraction 0.002. Where I think it breaks: feasibility_fraction 0.002 against feasible_tuples 20 over 10^4 tuples is exactly 20/10^4, so 28 certified instances arising from 20 feasible tuples means more than one instance came from some tuples and the DISTINCT-MINIMAL-MODEL DEDUPLICATION IS DOING LOAD-BEARING WORK. Re-derive that deduplication too. If a definition cannot be pinned from the frozen contract alone, SAY SO -- an unpinnable definition is itself the finding, and reporting one is worth more than guessing the producer's.
joints.breaking_artifact: Re-derived N_6(H) and feasibility fraction written before any blind_from path or producer report was opened, with the read order attested; on disagreement, the smallest b-tuple on which the two implementations differ.

joints.joint: J5 whether the R6 null object and the R7 known-false control actually discriminate
joints.attack_plan: Attack the controls as CONTROLS, not as records. (a) R7 known-false d = (1, 1, ...): the frozen expectation is certified totals n - 1. At n = 6 NOTHING WAS BUILT AT ALL (degenerate_deg_s_2 on all eight tuples) -- establish whether the known-false object was ever presented to the counted path, or whether it was rejected upstream by a filter the counted R3 path does not traverse. At n = 8 the totals [5, 6, 7, 7, 7, 7, 6, 7] straddle the expected 7 -- establish whether the deviations 5 and 6 are the control failing, the control being mis-specified against the closed form, or a genuine property of the degeneration at those tuples. (b) R6 null: found is [] and null_proof_first is null (PD-1), while the frozen contract required the infeasibility proof to be frozen in the run source BEFORE any R6 step. Establish whether R6's zero is informative or vacuous, and specifically whether the SAME degenerate_deg_s_2 rejection that emptied R7 and R8 also explains an empty R6. (c) R8 planted (IV-3): 0 of 9 plants built, recovered 0/0, slope null, decade_ratios {}. State plainly whether IV-3 was evaluated at all and whether a control that produced no objects can honestly be reported as anything other than NOT RUN. (d) THE DECISIVE TEST FOR THIS JOINT: exhibit, from the committed bytes at the snapshot commit (experiments/EXP-ECRANK-73275e/source/ and implementation.md are IN SCOPE for you and are blind_from only for the Validator), whether the code path that produced R3's 28 certified instances and the code path that produced the controls' zeros are THE SAME PATH. If they are not, no control covers the counted result and the round fails as a review of that result, regardless of the value 28. Objections and falsification routes only: run no arm, change no status, modify no raw artifact, and give every BLOCK item a worked falsification route.
joints.breaking_artifact: For each of R6, R7 and R8, a stated discrimination verdict (discriminates | does not discriminate | not run) with the artifact it is read from; plus the same-path / different-path finding for the counted versus control code paths, with the source line references that settle it.

joints.joint: J6 hidden assumptions, omitted end-to-end cost, and scope honesty
joints.attack_plan: (a) HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS. Enumerate every assumption the recorded numbers rest on that the frozen contract does not state. Start with PD-3: the n = 8 Bezout enumeration used the integer (a, b) box of width min(H, 20) rather than the full rational height-H coefficient lattice, so say exactly what quantity R5 therefore measured and what it did not, INDEPENDENTLY of the exhaustion. (b) OMITTED END-TO-END COST. counted_ops excludes RNG calls, Fraction-constructor gcd reductions and integer ops outside counted helpers per IC-1 [SR-11]: state whether counted_ops is therefore a LOWER bound on true cost and whether any recorded statement uses it as a bound in the other direction. Check wall_seconds_monotonic against wall_seconds_timestamp_span in all eight runs and report that they agree to six decimal places in every run, which is one instrument reported twice rather than the two independent measurements [SR-10] asks for. Check peak_rss_bytes (about 29-31 MB) against the declared 8 GB envelope and state the engine's real cost profile at n = 6 and n = 8, including what the 1.0e8-op wall at b_index 666 of 10000 implies about the cost of ever completing the declared n = 8 sample. (c) SCOPE HONESTY. Attack any language in the run records or the execution report that reads beyond the tested scope: beyond n in {6, 8}, beyond H <= 10^4 / 10^3, beyond the 10^4 seeded b-tuple sample, toward rank over Q, toward HEUR-1 being supported or refuted, toward C1, or toward any cryptographic scale. Attack in particular the cross-experiment comparison the contract sets up in P4: EV-ECRANK-8b35bb's 3e-4 bound is PER DRAW at n = 8 while R3's incidence is PER TUPLE at n = 6, and comparing them requires an assumption the contract does not supply -- name that assumption. joints.breaking_artifact: A numbered list of hidden assumptions and scope overreaches, each quoting the exact text or number and naming its artifact; plus a corrected statement of what R5 actually measured.

joints.joint: J7 the cheapest falsification control this result admits
joints.attack_plan: Name the SINGLE CHEAPEST artifact that would falsify the reading 'R3 exhibits 28 certified n = 6 instances', and say whether it can be computed from the committed bytes at snapshot 03c6e3181bc54b67ab3904b5f6187dbe4e6cb3ad WITHOUT re-running any arm. Price these explicitly, cheapest first: (i) re-verify the exhibited points of one recorded R3 instance against its Weierstrass equation in exact Fraction arithmetic with code independent of the producer's, and check non-torsion by Mazur -- an on-curve or torsion failure is a COUNTEREXAMPLE CERTIFICATE under docs/claims-and-verification.md 'Refutation artifacts' and is the strongest refutation artifact this result admits; (ii) check nonsingularity and the distinct-minimal-model deduplication across the 28, since 28 instances from 20 feasible tuples makes the deduplication load-bearing; (iii) feed one recorded R3 instance through the R7 known-false path and one R7 d = (1, 1, ...) object through the R3 counted path, which settles J5's same-path question mechanically. Deliver the ranked list with a cost estimate for each, state which one you actually ran, and give its outcome. If none can be computed from committed bytes, say so plainly and name exactly what a successor task would need.

blindness.within_round: TASK-20260907-d47eb0 (Validator) and TASK-20260907-46731e (Red Team) run CONCURRENTLY in separate independent sessions and may NOT read each other's task directory, report, or attestation. Each attests in review_attestation.yaml to exactly what it read, with read_sibling_reports false. Both read the SAME snapshot-bound producer artifacts at 03c6e3181bc54b67ab3904b5f6187dbe4e6cb3ad and the frozen contract. Neither reviewer returns a whole-claim verdict: each reports on its own joints, and the Coordinator composes them in TASK-20260907-175a4a. A blinded reviewer cannot see the other joints by construction, so a whole-claim verdict from one would be an opinion formed from a fraction of the evidence.

objects: The known-false Mestre degeneration d = (1, 1, ..., 1) of R7 (seed 760812) at n = 6 and n = 8, whose frozen closed form fixes certified totals at exactly n - 1 (5 and 7). The certification pipeline that produced R3's 28 must NOT report a certified instance above n - 1 on this family.

The R6 null family: the n = 6 quadratic with its constant term sign-forced so that no rational in-box solution can exist, frozen in experiments/EXP-ECRANK-73275e/source/null_family.py before any R6 step. The solver must return exactly 0 solutions AND the audit code must flag the infeasibility.

The degenerate_deg_s_2 rejection itself, treated as a null object. Whatever rejected all eight R7 n = 6 tuples and all nine R8 plants must be shown to lie on the SAME code path that accepted R3's 28. A rejection that only the control objects ever meet is not a control.
proves_too_much.failure_signature: The argument proves too much if ANY of the following holds. (a) The pipeline reports a certified instance above n - 1 on the d = (1, 1, ...) family, or a nonzero solution set on the R6 null family: the conclusion goes through where it is known false. (b) The controls' zeros are produced by a rejection path (degenerate_deg_s_2) that the counted R3 path never traverses, so no control could have failed whatever the counted path did -- a control that cannot fail is not a control, and docs/inventor-protocol.md treats a quantity that fails to move when the parameter meant to destroy it is applied as the canonical artifact tell. (c) IV-3's planted family produced no plants at all, so the positive control never evaluated. Any of (a), (b) or (c) means this round FAILS as a review of the counted result, regardless of the value 28 and regardless of every other joint's verdict.

blind_rederivation.quantity: N_6(H), the construct_count of experiments/EXP-ECRANK-73275e/specification.yaml metrics.primary -- the number of distinct-minimal-model certified instances (nonsingular, twist class populated, certified rank above the trivial) at each nested box height H in {10^2, 10^3, 10^4} for the n = 6 arm -- together with the feasibility fraction, the fraction of the declared 10^4 b-tuples having at least one in-box solution of the single n - 5 = 1 quadratic ellipticity condition. The re-deriver starts from this STATEMENT and the parameters below, never from the producer's method.
blind_rederivation.parameters: n = 6; seed 760806 via random.Random(760806); 10^4 b-tuples in affine normal form b1 = 0, b2 = 1, b3..b6 distinct integers in [-20, 20] excluding {0, 1}, seeded order with no adaptive reordering; support {-1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13}; square pattern prescribed on the carrier coordinate r_n; nested cumulative coefficient boxes H in {10^2, 10^3, 10^4}; exact rational arithmetic with fractions.Fraction, stdlib only; no descent, no PARI, no network; counted exact-op cap 1.0e8.
blind_rederivation.read_order_requirement: experiments/EXP-ECRANK-73275e/execution-report.yaml and experiments/EXP-ECRANK-73275e/runs/RUN-ECRANK-73275e-R3-construct-n6/raw-result.json and .../RUN-ECRANK-73275e-R4-construct-n6-replay/raw-result.json are NOT in blind_from, because joints J1 and J2 require the Validator to check raw-versus-summary agreement against exactly those files. The compensating control is a DECLARED READ ORDER: the J4 re-derivation and its numbers are written into validation-report.md BEFORE any of those three files is opened, and review_attestation.yaml records the read order explicitly. This limit is declared here, in advance, rather than discovered afterwards; it is a stated weakening of blindness for the number 28 only, and it is the price of giving one reviewer both the integrity duty and the re-derivation duty.
blind_rederivation.blindness_limits: blind_from covers the producer's IMPLEMENTATION (source/ and implementation.md), which is what the review-architecture contract names and what a wrong-but-self-consistent implementation would hide in. It does not cover the producer's raw records, for the reason stated in read_order_requirement.
